subject: Log Scale in a barplot with fill

messages.author: 3c9c3a677d88c607
messages.subject: Log Scale in a barplot with fill
parts:
Dear List,

I want to create a barplot with a log10 transformed y-scale. As long
as there is only one variable, everything goes fine:

td <- data.frame(d=c(rep("a", 100), rep("b", 1000), rep("c",
1000000)))
pl <- ggplot(td)

pl + geom_bar(mapping=aes(x=d, y=..count..)) + scale_y_log10()

This produces exactly what I would expect.

However once the dataframe contains a second variable and this
variable is mapped to "fill" strange things happen once the
scale_y_log10() is added:

td <- data.frame(d=c(rep("a", 100), rep("b", 1000), rep("c",
1000000)), l=sample(c("x","y"), 1001100, replace=T))

pl <- ggplot(td)
pl + geom_bar(mapping=aes(x=d, y=..count.., fill=l)) # Works,
but you can hardly see categories "a" and "b"
pl + geom_bar(mapping=aes(x=d, y=..count.., fill=l)) +
scale_y_log10() # Something seems to go wrong here. The total count
of "c" appears to be somewhere near 10^11. The same thing seems to
happen to the other categories

I thought of using coord_trans instead of scale_y_log10 but it throws
an error I can't really interpret:

pl + geom_bar(mapping=aes(x=d, y=..count.., fill=l)) +
coord_trans(ytrans="log10")

Error in if (length(from) == 1 || abs(from[1] - from[2]) < 1e-06)
return(mean(to)) :
missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed

Can anyone give me a hint on what could be my mistake here?

Thanks a lot

Sebastian

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Log Scale in a barplot with fill
parts:
Hi:

I don't think you did anything wrong AFAICT. Since I'm not a big fan of stacked bar plots (I tend to prefer dodging myself, particularly with small numbers of subgroups as is the case here), an alternative is to use position = 'dodge' instead, which circumvents the problem in the interim:

pl + geom_bar(aes(x=d, fill = l), position = 'dodge') + scale_y_log10()

Sheer guess:  10^5 * 10^5 = 10^10, when what was needed was k1 * 10^5 + k2 * 10^5 = (k1 + k2) * 10^5.  I don't have the courage to hack that code, though :)

HTH,
Dennis

Actually it's a bug that this works at all - the base of the bars lies
on y = 0, which on the log scale is -oo, so I'm surprised you don't
get an error. Bar charts and log axes do not mix well.
